Fire, security & access

Fire doors, hardware and agreed access or security work coordinated with your site team.

THE BRIEF

We organise defined maintenance and rectification with the site manager and relevant service providers. We identify the door, equipment or system involved and review existing defect and service records. Inspection, repair, testing and certification remain separately identified parts of the agreed scope.

✺

THE WORK

Three related areas, clearly defined

  • Fire doors and associated hardware

    We review the identified door, closer, hinges, latch and existing defect report. The door assembly and relevant records inform which repair can be included.

  • Access control and locks

    We identify the affected entrance, hardware and operating issue. Existing equipment details and site arrangements guide the proposed repair and any system coordination.

  • Agreed security equipment

    We define the equipment and work required for the premises. Separate servicing or attendance is arranged where the scope needs the relevant provider.

THE WORK

A door fault is more than one loose part

  • Alignment and operation

    A door that does not close or latch may involve the leaf, frame, hinges, closer or fixing condition. We inspect how these parts work together before specifying hardware.

  • Matching the assembly

    We check available product identification and existing documentation. Appearance alone is not a sufficient basis for selecting a replacement within a specified door or access system.

Prepare the temporary access before attendance

    We review the equipment, reported problem, requested work and the records required for that scope.

    We document completed work and the relevant operating checks, then hand over the applicable records and any further items.

THE WORK

A scope that distinguishes the different tasks

  • Equipment and components

    Door quantities, hardware identification, retained components, access equipment and product availability affect preparation and attendance.

  • Inspection and documentation

    The quotation identifies the agreed repair and any separately arranged inspection, servicing, testing or certification, including the relevant attendance.

THE WORK

Handover by entrance, item and status

We link completed items to the door or equipment identifier. The record distinguishes the work performed, checks undertaken, documents supplied and items awaiting a further decision. Your manager can see which entrances are back in use, what records have been supplied and which items still need a separate visit.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Can a closer be repaired without replacing the whole door?+

We first check the door, frame, hinges, fixing condition and the closer. The proposed work must suit the assembly and existing records, so the scope follows that assessment.

How do occupants enter during the work?+

We agree a practical temporary arrangement with your site representative before attendance, including any affected entrances and system interruptions. The plan depends on the actual building layout and work.

Are repair records the same as certification?+

They serve different purposes. We identify the repair record and any separate inspection, test or certification required for the agreed work, with the relevant service attendance clearly stated.

Can you include fire door repairs in a maintenance visit?+

We review the door, hardware, defect report and required work first. We then confirm the appropriate repair scope and documentation, and coordinate any separate inspection or service attendance that the work requires.
